body:
## Problem

`yarn.lock` resolves `postcss` to 8.5.14 and `brace-expansion` to 5.0.7, both
of which carry HIGH-severity advisories with published fixes. `postcss` is a
**direct** dependency of this package, so the vulnerable version is attributed
to `@ivuorinen/stylelint-config` itself and propagates into every consumer's
tree.

## Evidence

Three independent scanners agree.

`yarn npm audit --recursive --severity moderate`:
```
├─ postcss
│  ├─ Issue: PostCSS: Path Traversal in Previous Source Map Auto-Loading
│  │         (sourceMappingURL) leads to Arbitrary .map File Disclosure
│  ├─ URL: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849
│  ├─ Severity: high
│  ├─ Vulnerable Versions: <=8.5.17
│  ├─ Tree Versions: 8.5.14
│  └─ Dependents: @ivuorinen/stylelint-config@workspace:.
├─ brace-expansion
│  ├─ Issue: DoS via unbounded expansion length causing an OOM process crash
│  ├─ URL: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg
│  ├─ Severity: high
│  ├─ Vulnerable Versions: <=5.0.7
│  └─ Dependents: minimatch@npm:10.2.4
```

`trivy fs --scanners vuln`:
```
│ postcss │ GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 │ HIGH │ fixed │ 8.5.14 │ 8.5.18 │
```

`grype dir:.`:
```
postcss  8.5.14  8.5.18  npm  GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849  High
```

`yarn.lock` confirms the resolution:
```
"postcss@npm:^8.5.8":
  version: 8.5.14
```

The declared range `^8.5.8` already permits 8.5.18, and `resolutions`
already pins `brace-expansion: ^5.0.7` which permits 5.0.8 — so both are pure
lockfile staleness, not range constraints. Open update branches exist and are
unmerged: `origin/dependabot/npm_and_yarn/postcss-8.5.18`,
`origin/renovate/npm-postcss-vulnerability`,
`origin/dependabot/npm_and_yarn/brace-expansion-5.0.8`,
`origin/renovate/npm-brace-expansion-vulnerability`.

## Impact

A consumer installing `@ivuorinen/stylelint-config` pulls postcss 8.5.14. Any
CSS the consumer lints that carries a crafted `/*# sourceMappingURL=... */`
comment can make postcss read an arbitrary `.map` file off the linting host
and surface its contents. In CI that host holds the consumer's checkout and
often credentials. The advisory is reachable from ordinary use of this package
because postcss is exactly what stylelint feeds untrusted CSS to.

## Fix

Refresh the lockfile so both resolve to fixed versions — no manifest range
change is needed:

```sh
yarn up postcss@^8.5.18 brace-expansion@^5.0.8
```

Then merge (or close in favour of the refreshed lock) the four open
update branches. Separately, drop the direct `postcss` dependency entirely —
see the `deps` finding on unused direct dependencies; that removes this
package as the attributed dependent.

## Resolution
Raised resolutions to brace-expansion ^5.0.8 and added postcss ^8.5.18; dependency floor also raised to ^8.5.18. yarn.lock now resolves postcss 8.5.22 and brace-expansion 5.0.8. 'yarn npm audit --recursive --severity high' returns 'No audit suggestions' (was 2 HIGH). Only remaining advisory is tar (moderate) via npm@11.11.0 in the dev tree, absent from the published closure.
title: Lockfile ships two HIGH advisories with fixes already available

body:
## Problem

`package.json` declares `"stylelint": "^17.6.0"` under `dependencies`. A
shareable stylelint config must declare stylelint as a `peerDependency`: it
does not *use* stylelint, it is *consumed by* it. As a hard dependency the
version relationship with the consumer's stylelint becomes unchecked and
unreported, and a second copy of stylelint is installed into every consumer
tree.

Every sibling package in this same dependency graph gets this right:

| package | stylelint declared as |
| --- | --- |
| `stylelint-config-standard@40` | `peerDependencies: {"stylelint": "^17.0.0"}` |
| `stylelint-config-recommended-scss@17` | `peerDependencies: {"stylelint": "^17.0.0"}` |
| `stylelint-order@8.1.1` | `peerDependencies: {"stylelint": "^16.18.0 \|\| ^17.0.0"}` |
| `stylelint-scss@7` | `peerDependencies: {"stylelint": "^16.8.2 \|\| ^17.0.0"}` |
| `@ivuorinen/stylelint-config` | `dependencies` |

## Evidence

Packed the current tree and installed it alongside `stylelint@16` in a clean
fixture:

```sh
npm pack --pack-destination $SP
cd $SP && npm i --no-audit --no-fund -D stylelint@16 ./ivuorinen-stylelint-config-1.0.21.tgz
```

Install succeeded with **no peer warning of any kind** (grepped the install
output for `peer|ERESOLVE`: no matches), and produced two stylelints:

```
node_modules/stylelint                                       -> 16.26.1
node_modules/@ivuorinen/stylelint-config/node_modules/stylelint -> 17.14.1
```

The two are resolved by different consumers:

```
CLI / consumer resolves:  .../node_modules/stylelint/lib/index.cjs        (16.26.1)
our package resolves:     .../@ivuorinen/stylelint-config/node_modules/
                            stylelint/lib/index.mjs                       (17.14.1)
```

Contrast: `stylelint-config-standard@40` in the same tree declares
`peer: {"stylelint": "^17.0.0"}`, so npm has something to check — but our hard
dependency silently absorbs the 16-vs-17 mismatch before it can surface.

## Impact

1. **Silent version mismatch.** A consumer on an unsupported stylelint gets no
   install-time signal. The rule set in this config is validated against the
   stylelint the *consumer* runs, so a rule that exists in 17 but not in the
   consumer's stylelint fails at lint time as `Unknown rule` — exactly the
   class of failure this package just shipped in 1.3.5 — instead of as a peer
   error at install time.
2. **Install bloat.** Every consumer downloads and stores a second full
   stylelint (17.14.1 above) that nothing executes.
3. **Duplicated CVE surface.** The nested copy has its own transitive tree that
   the consumer's audit tooling must patch separately.

## Fix

Move stylelint out of `dependencies` and into `peerDependencies`, matching the
range the config's own `extends` chain requires (`stylelint-config-standard@40`
requires `^17.0.0`):

```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "stylelint": "^17.0.0"
},
"dependencies": {
  "@ivuorinen/config-checker": "^2.2.1",
  "stylelint-config-recommended-scss": "^17.0.0",
  "stylelint-config-standard": "^40.0.0",
  "stylelint-order": "^8.1.1",
  "stylelint-scss": "^7.0.0"
},
"devDependencies": {
  "@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config": "^1.2.1",
  "stylelint": "^17.6.0"
}
```

Keep it in `devDependencies` so `test/smoke.mjs` and local runs still have a
stylelint to execute. Then extend `test/smoke.mjs` to assert the fixture
contains exactly one `node_modules/**/stylelint/package.json`, so a
regression back to `dependencies` fails CI.

## Resolution
stylelint moved from dependencies to peerDependencies ^17.0.0, plus devDependencies ^17.6.0 for local runs. test/smoke.mjs now asserts the packed manifest declares it as a peer and not a dependency, and that the consumer tree contains exactly one stylelint. Verified: reverting to dependencies makes the suite exit 1.
title: stylelint is a hard dependency, not a peerDependency

body:
## Problem

`scripts/postinstall.cjs` reads `process.env.INIT_CWD` and passes it straight
into `path.join` without checking it exists. `INIT_CWD` is an npm/yarn
convention, not a Node or POSIX guarantee. When it is absent the script dies
with an unhandled `TypeError`, and because it is a `postinstall` hook that
aborts the consumer's install.

```js
const filePath = path.join(process.env.INIT_CWD, '.stylelintrc.json')
```

The `checkConfig('stylelint')` call on line 10 dereferences it first and fails
even earlier.

## Evidence

```sh
$ cd /tmp && env -u INIT_CWD node scripts/postinstall.cjs
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "path" argument must be of type string.
Received undefined
    at Object.join (node:path:1339:7)
    at .../@ivuorinen/config-checker/lib/config-checker.js:29:55
    at Array.filter (<anonymous>)
    at configChecker (.../config-checker.js:29:19)
    at Object.<anonymous> (.../scripts/postinstall.cjs:10:21)
```

The file's own eslint header shows the hazard was noticed but not handled:

```js
/* eslint no-console: "off", n/no-process-exit: "off", no-undefined: "off" -- CLI app that gives users feedback */
```

## Impact

Any install path that does not set `INIT_CWD` fails hard with a stack trace
instead of skipping a cosmetic convenience step. Reachable via `npm rebuild`,
a direct `node node_modules/@ivuorinen/stylelint-config/scripts/postinstall.cjs`,
a container build that copies `node_modules` and re-runs lifecycle scripts, or
any third-party installer that does not implement the npm-specific `INIT_CWD`
convention. Writing a default `.stylelintrc.json` is a nicety; taking down the
install for it is not an acceptable failure mode.

## Fix

Bail out quietly when the variable is missing — the script's whole purpose is
optional convenience:

```js
const initCwd = process.env.INIT_CWD

if (!initCwd) {
  console.log('stylelint-config: INIT_CWD not set, skipping config creation.')
  process.exit(0)
}

const foundConfig = checkConfig('stylelint')
```

Note the ordering: the guard must precede the `checkConfig` call, which is
where the current crash originates. Cover it in `test/smoke.mjs` by invoking
the script with `INIT_CWD` deleted from the env and asserting exit 0.

## Resolution
postinstall now reads INIT_CWD into a local, exits 0 with a log line when unset, and reads the manifest inside try/catch. test/smoke.mjs runs the script with INIT_CWD deleted and asserts exit 0. Note the guard is now belt-and-braces: the try/catch alone also prevents the abort, so removing the guard does not reintroduce the crash. The test asserts the requirement (never abort an install), not the specific guard.
title: postinstall aborts the install with a raw TypeError when INIT_CWD is unset

body:
## Problem

MegaLinter enables `JAVASCRIPT_ES` and `TYPESCRIPT_ES` and points both at a
config file that does not exist in the repository. The config that *does*
exist imports a package that is declared nowhere and installed nowhere. The
JS/TS lint gate is therefore dead: it is switched on, reported as a check, and
cannot evaluate a single rule.

## Evidence

`.mega-linter.yml`:
```yaml
ENABLE_LINTERS:
  - JAVASCRIPT_ES
  - TYPESCRIPT_ES

JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE: .eslintrc.json
TYPESCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE: .eslintrc.json
```

The file is absent:
```sh
$ ls -la .eslintrc.json
ls: cannot access '.eslintrc.json': No such file or directory
```

The real config is `eslint.config.mjs`, which begins:
```js
import ivuorinenConfig from '@ivuorinen/eslint-config';
```

`@ivuorinen/eslint-config` appears nowhere in `package.json`:
```sh
$ grep -n 'eslint' package.json
NOT in package.json
$ ls -d node_modules/@ivuorinen/*
node_modules/@ivuorinen/config-checker
node_modules/@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config
```

So `eslint .` cannot resolve its own config, and MegaLinter is looking for a
different file entirely.

## Impact

The repository has a JS lint gate in name only, on a package whose entire
shipped surface is four JavaScript files. Nothing checks them. The gate is
also wired into the release path — `publish.yml`'s `Linter` job is a `needs:`
of `publish` — so a green release signal is being produced by a check that
never inspected the code.

## Fix

Two changes, both required:

1. Point MegaLinter at the flat config, or drop the override so it
   auto-detects `eslint.config.mjs`:
   ```yaml
   # .mega-linter.yml — delete both lines; MegaLinter finds eslint.config.mjs itself
   -JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE: .eslintrc.json
   -TYPESCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE: .eslintrc.json
   ```
2. Declare the config package so ESLint can resolve it:
   ```sh
   yarn add -D @ivuorinen/eslint-config eslint
   ```

Then verify locally with `yarn eslint .` before trusting the CI check again.
If the intent is that this repo has no ESLint gate, the honest change is to
remove `JAVASCRIPT_ES`/`TYPESCRIPT_ES` from `ENABLE_LINTERS` and delete
`eslint.config.mjs` — but do not leave an enabled linter that cannot run.

## Resolution
Removed JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE / TYPESCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE from .mega-linter.yml so MegaLinter auto-detects eslint.config.mjs, and declared @ivuorinen/eslint-config ^1.4.0 + eslint ^10.7.0 as devDependencies. 'yarn eslint .' now runs and exits 0. It immediately found 20 real errors in the new test file (no-console, object-shorthand, no-undefined, no-restricted-properties, require-unicode-regexp), all fixed rather than suppressed — except no-console, disabled file-scope with justification, matching the existing precedent in scripts/postinstall.cjs. eslint ^10.8.0 was rejected by yarn's npmMinimalAgeGate (1440 min); ^10.7.0 is the newest aged-in release.
title: The JavaScript lint gate cannot run: config file absent, config package undeclared

body:
## Problem

`test/smoke.mjs` only ever asserts that stylelint **exits 0** and prints no
`Unknown rule`. It never asserts that the config enforces anything. A config
whose `rules` object is empty — or silently emptied by a bad merge, a wrong
`extends` resolution, or a future `normalizeAllRuleSettings` change — passes
every one of the six cases. The test proves "the config loads", not "the config
lints".

## Evidence

Replaced `css/index.cjs` with a config carrying zero rules:

```js
'use strict'

module.exports = {
  extends: ['stylelint-config-standard'],
  plugins: ['stylelint-order'],
  rules: {}
}
```

Then ran the suite unmodified:

```
$ node test/smoke.mjs
✔ @ivuorinen/stylelint-config → a.css (extends string)
✔ @ivuorinen/stylelint-config → a.css (imported object)
✔ @ivuorinen/stylelint-config/css → a.css (extends string)
✔ @ivuorinen/stylelint-config/css → a.css (imported object)
✔ @ivuorinen/stylelint-config/scss → a.scss (extends string)
✔ @ivuorinen/stylelint-config/scss → a.scss (imported object)

All specifiers lint clean.
EXIT=0
```

Six green checks, zero rules configured. The assertions are one-sided: every
check is a *negative* (no error, no unknown rule), so deleting enforcement can
only make the suite greener.

## Impact

The test was added specifically to stop a broken config from shipping, and it
is blind to the most direct way a config breaks — losing its rules. It gates
`publish` in `publish.yml`, so it converts a silently-gutted config into a
green release.

## Fix

Add a negative fixture per specifier: a file that the config **must** reject,
asserted to exit non-zero and to name the expected rule. This makes the suite
two-sided.

```js
// must-fail fixtures: exit 0 here means the rule set is gone
const BAD_CSS = '#id-sel {\n  color: red;\n}\n'   // selector-max-id: 0 + color-named: never
const BAD_SCSS = '$C: 1px;\n'                     // scss/dollar-variable-pattern

const negatives = [
  { file: 'bad.css', extend: PKG, rule: 'selector-max-id' },
  { file: 'bad.css', extend: `${PKG}/css`, rule: 'selector-max-id' },
  { file: 'bad.scss', extend: `${PKG}/scss`, rule: 'scss/dollar-variable-pattern' }
]

for (const { file, extend, rule } of negatives) {
  fs.rmSync(rcMjs, { force: true })
  fs.writeFileSync(rcJson, JSON.stringify({ extends: [extend] }))
  const result = spawnSync(bin, [file], { cwd: fixture, encoding: 'utf8' })
  const output = `${result.stdout}${result.stderr}`

  check(() => {
    assert.notEqual(result.status, 0, `${extend} on ${file}: expected a violation, got exit 0 — rule set may be empty\n${output}`)
    assert.match(output, new RegExp(rule), `${extend} on ${file}: expected ${rule} to fire\n${output}`)
    assert.doesNotMatch(output, /Unknown rule/, `${extend} on ${file}: unknown rules\n${output}`)
  })
}
```

Verify the fix by re-running the gutted-config experiment above: it must now
fail.

## Resolution
Added a dirty fixture per specifier (dirty.css with #id-sel + color:red, dirty.scss with $BadName) asserted to exit non-zero and name the expected rule. Verified: emptying css/index.cjs rules now makes the suite exit 1, where it previously passed 6/6.
title: Smoke test passes with the entire rule set deleted

body:
## Problem

`test/smoke.mjs` installs stylelint by bare name:

```js
run('npm', [
  'install',
  '--no-audit',
  '--no-fund',
  '--save-dev',
  'stylelint',
  path.join(fixture, tarball)
])
```

A bare `stylelint` resolves to the `latest` dist-tag, which has no relationship
to the `^17.6.0` this package declares. The test therefore validates the config
against whatever major npm happens to serve on the day CI runs.

## Evidence

```sh
$ npm view stylelint dist-tags
{ latest: '17.14.1' }
```

Today `latest` (17.14.1) happens to satisfy `^17.6.0`, so the test is
accidentally correct. The day stylelint 18.0.0 publishes, the same unchanged
test installs 18 at the fixture top level while the tarball's own
`dependencies` drag in a nested 17 (the duplicate-install mechanism proven in
`deps-d7bddd01`). The CLI at `node_modules/.bin/stylelint` is then 18, linting
a rule set authored for 17.

Two failure directions, both bad:
- 18 removes another batch of rules → the suite goes red on a day nobody
  touched the repo, and the red says "Unknown rule" as though the config
  regressed.
- 18 keeps every rule → the suite goes green while having tested an
  unsupported, undeclared combination.

## Impact

The suite gates `publish`. A stylelint release the maintainer has not opted
into can either block all releases or silently change what "tested" means.
Neither is a property you want in a release gate.

## Fix

Install the range the package actually declares, read from `package.json` so
the two can never drift:

```js
const manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(repo, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
const stylelintRange = manifest.peerDependencies?.stylelint
  ?? manifest.devDependencies?.stylelint
  ?? manifest.dependencies?.stylelint

assert.ok(stylelintRange, 'package.json declares no stylelint version to test against')

run('npm', [
  'install',
  '--no-audit',
  '--no-fund',
  '--save-dev',
  `stylelint@${stylelintRange}`,
  path.join(fixture, tarball)
])
```

Widening support to a new stylelint major then becomes a deliberate manifest
edit that the test follows, rather than something the registry decides.

## Resolution
The suite now reads the stylelint range from package.json (peerDependencies first, then devDependencies, then dependencies) and installs stylelint@<range>, asserting the manifest declares one at all. Widening to a new stylelint major is now a deliberate manifest edit rather than a registry decision.
title: Smoke test installs stylelint@latest, not the version range the package declares

body:
## Problem

`publish.yml` sets the npm publish token as a **workflow-level** `env`, which
GitHub injects into every job and every step in the file — including jobs that
have no business holding a publish credential.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/publish.yml:15-16
env:
  NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

## Evidence

Three jobs run in this workflow, and all three inherit `NPM_TOKEN`:

| job | needs the token? | what it runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Linter` | no | `ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint@94a4f68…` — a third-party composite action |
| `Test` | no | `node test/smoke.mjs`, which shells out to `npm pack` / `npm install` |
| `publish` | yes | `cycjimmy/semantic-release-action@b12c8f6…` |

The one place the token is genuinely required already sets it explicitly at
step scope:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/publish.yml:100-104
      - name: Semantic Release
        uses: cycjimmy/semantic-release-action@b12c8f6015dc215fe37bc154d4ad456dd3833c90 # v6.0.0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

So the workflow-level declaration is redundant on top of being over-broad.
`zizmor` reports clean here — it does not model env-scope breadth — so this is
not covered by the existing scanner gate.

## Impact

The credential that can publish `@ivuorinen/stylelint-config` to npm is placed
in the environment of a third-party composite action and of a job that runs
`npm install` against the public registry. Both are pinned by SHA, which
narrows but does not remove the exposure: a compromise of the pinned tree, or
any transitive install script running in the `Test` job, reads `NPM_TOKEN`
from `process.env` and can publish arbitrary package versions under this name.
Least privilege for a publish token is the publish step and nothing else.

## Fix

Delete the workflow-level block. No other change is needed — the publish step
already has what it needs.

```diff
 permissions: {}

-env:
-  NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
-
 jobs:
```

Confirm afterwards that a release still succeeds; the `Semantic Release` step's
own `env:` is what `semantic-release` reads.

## Resolution
Deleted the workflow-level env block from publish.yml, leaving NPM_TOKEN scoped to the Semantic Release step that already declared it. The Linter and Test jobs no longer receive the publish credential. actionlint and zizmor still pass.
title: NPM_TOKEN is exposed at workflow level to every job, including third-party actions

body:
## Problem

`package.json` declares `"engines": {"node": ">=20"}`. Every stylelint package
in the dependency chain requires `>=20.19.0`. A consumer on Node 20.0–20.18
satisfies this package's declared engine and then fails its dependencies'.

## Evidence

```
stylelint                              {"node":">=20.19.0"}
stylelint-config-standard              {"node":">=20.19.0"}
stylelint-config-recommended-scss      {"node":">=20"}
stylelint-order                        {"node":">=20.19.0"}
stylelint-scss                         {"node":">=20.19.0"}
@ivuorinen/config-checker              undefined
OURS                                   {"node":">=20"}
```

Four of the five direct stylelint dependencies require `>=20.19.0`. Node 20.11
and 20.18 are real, widely-pinned LTS point releases that pass `>=20` and fail
`>=20.19.0`.

`.nvmrc` is `v24`, so CI never exercises the range this package claims to
support — the gap is invisible to the existing pipeline.

## Impact

A consumer pinned to Node 20.18 installs the package, gets `EBADENGINE`
warnings from four transitive packages (or a hard failure under
`engine-strict=true`), and the manifest they consulted told them Node 20 was
fine. The declared contract is wrong in the direction that costs the consumer
debugging time.

## Fix

Match the floor the dependency chain actually imposes:

```diff
   "engines": {
-    "node": ">=20"
+    "node": ">=20.19.0"
   },
```

If supporting earlier Node 20 matters, the alternative is to pin the stylelint
chain back to versions with a `>=20` floor — but that means giving up
stylelint 17, so raising the declared floor is the correct direction.

## Resolution
engines.node raised from >=20 to >=20.19.0, matching stylelint, stylelint-config-standard, stylelint-order and stylelint-scss.
title: engines.node understates the real floor by 19 patch releases

body:
## Problem

`scripts/postinstall.cjs` writes `.stylelintrc.json` into `process.env.INIT_CWD`
— the directory where the *user's* install command was invoked, not the
directory of the package that depends on this one. There is no environment
variable, flag, or config key to suppress it.

```js
const filePath = path.join(process.env.INIT_CWD, '.stylelintrc.json')
const fileConfigObject = {
  extends: ['@ivuorinen/stylelint-config/css']
}

if (!fs.existsSync(filePath)) {
  fs.writeFileSync(filePath, JSON.stringify(fileConfigObject, undefined, 2))
}
```

## Evidence

Reproduced in a clean fixture that asked for nothing but the tarball:

```sh
$ mkdir repro && cd repro && npm init -y
$ npm i -D stylelint ./ivuorinen-stylelint-config-1.0.21.tgz
$ cat .stylelintrc.json
{
  "extends": [
    "@ivuorinen/stylelint-config/css"
  ]
}
```

`INIT_CWD` is the top-level invocation directory regardless of install depth.
So when package `A` depends on this config and a user runs `npm i A`, the file
lands in the *user's* repository root — a repo whose author never chose this
config and may not use stylelint at all.

The `@ivuorinen/config-checker` guard only skips when a stylelint config is
already present; it does not distinguish a direct install from a transitive
one:

```js
const foundConfig = checkConfig('stylelint')

if (foundConfig.length > 0) { ...skip... }
```

## Impact

An install of an unrelated package mutates the consumer's working tree. In the
best case it is a spurious untracked file; in a repo with a `pre-commit` gate
or a `git status --porcelain` check in CI, it is a failing build with no
obvious cause. Writing to a directory outside the package's own tree during
`postinstall` is a side effect a dependency should not take unasked.

## Fix

Only write when this package is a **direct** dependency of the project being
installed. `INIT_CWD`'s own `package.json` is the authority:

```js
const initCwd = process.env.INIT_CWD

if (!initCwd) {
  console.log('stylelint-config: INIT_CWD not set, skipping config creation.')
  process.exit(0)
}

if (process.env.IVUORINEN_STYLELINT_NO_POSTINSTALL) {
  console.log('stylelint-config: opt-out set, skipping config creation.')
  process.exit(0)
}

const PKG = '@ivuorinen/stylelint-config'
let manifest = {}

try {
  manifest = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(initCwd, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
} catch {
  console.log('stylelint-config: no readable package.json at INIT_CWD, skipping.')
  process.exit(0)
}

const isDirect = Boolean(
  manifest.dependencies?.[PKG] ||
    manifest.devDependencies?.[PKG] ||
    manifest.peerDependencies?.[PKG]
)

if (!isDirect) {
  console.log(`stylelint-config: ${PKG} is a transitive dependency here, skipping config creation.`)
  process.exit(0)
}
```

The `INIT_CWD` guard here is the same one `errors-767bc7a4` requires — fix both
together. Document the `IVUORINEN_STYLELINT_NO_POSTINSTALL` opt-out in the
README (see `docs` findings), and cover the transitive case in
`test/smoke.mjs` with a fixture whose `package.json` does not list the package.

## Resolution
postinstall now reads INIT_CWD's package.json and writes only when @ivuorinen/stylelint-config appears in its dependencies/devDependencies/peerDependencies, plus an IVUORINEN_STYLELINT_NO_POSTINSTALL opt-out. test/smoke.mjs asserts no file is written into a fixture that does not depend on the package. Verified: removing the guard makes the suite exit 1. Documented in the README.
title: postinstall writes into the top-level project on transitive installs, with no opt-out

body:
## Problem

The per-case success line is guarded by the run-wide `failures` counter rather
than by whether *this* case passed:

```js
      check(() => {
        assert.doesNotMatch(output, /Unknown rule/, `${label}: unknown rules\n${output}`)
        assert.equal(result.status, 0, `${label}: exit ${result.status}\n${output}`)
      })

      if (failures === 0) console.log(`✔ ${label}`)
```

Once any case fails, `failures` is non-zero for the rest of the run and no
further `✔` prints — including for cases that did pass.

## Evidence

Observed while verifying the suite detects a reintroduced bug. Restoring the
bare relative `extends` in `scss/index.cjs` produced:

```
✔ @ivuorinen/stylelint-config → a.css (extends string)
✔ @ivuorinen/stylelint-config/css → a.css (extends string)
EXIT=1
```

Six cases run. Two `✔` lines appeared, one `✖` was printed to stderr, and the
three remaining cases — two of which passed — produced no output at all. The
transcript makes it look as though the run aborted at case three.

## Impact

On a red CI run the log understates coverage: a maintainer reading it cannot
tell whether the later specifiers were tested and passed, or never ran. That is
exactly the information needed to localise which entry point broke.

## Fix

Have `check` report whether it passed, and gate the line on that:

```js
const check = (fn) => {
  try {
    fn()
    return true
  } catch (error) {
    failures += 1
    console.error(`✖ ${error.message}`)
    return false
  }
}
```

then at each call site:

```js
      const ok = check(() => {
        assert.doesNotMatch(output, /Unknown rule/, `${label}: unknown rules\n${output}`)
        assert.equal(result.status, 0, `${label}: exit ${result.status}\n${output}`)
      })

      if (ok) console.log(`✔ ${label}`)
```

## Resolution
check() now returns true/false and each call site prints its own tick, so a failure no longer suppresses success lines for later cases.
title: Success lines are gated on the global failure counter, hiding which cases passed

## Problem

The README's license reference resolves to `./LICENSE`; the file in the
repository is `LICENSE.md`.

## Evidence

```sh
$ ls LICENSE LICENSE.md
ls: cannot access 'LICENSE': No such file or directory
LICENSE.md

$ grep -n 'LICENSE' README.md
101:Distributed under the MIT License. See [LICENSE][license-link] for more information.
109:[license-link]: ./LICENSE
```

`license-link` is used twice — once in the prose on line 101 and once as the
href behind the license badge in the header block.

## Impact

Both the badge and the "See LICENSE" link 404 on GitHub and on the npm package
page. For a package whose only legal statement is that link, a dead target is
worth fixing.

```diff
-[license-link]: ./LICENSE
+[license-link]: ./LICENSE.md
```

body:
## Problem

The `Extending the config` section demonstrates `at-rule-no-unknown` with an
`ignoreAtRules` list naming two at-rules that exist in no CSS dialect this
package supports.

```json
{
  "extends": ["@ivuorinen/stylelint-config/css", "some-other-config-you-use"],
  "rules": {
    "at-rule-no-unknown": [
      true,
      {
        "ignoreAtRules": ["extends", "ignores"]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Evidence

`README.md:80`:
```
        "ignoreAtRules": ["extends", "ignores"]
```

- `@extends` is not an at-rule. SCSS defines `@extend` (singular); the plural
  form matches nothing.
- `@ignores` is not an at-rule in CSS, SCSS, Less, PostCSS, or Tailwind.

So a reader who copies the example configures `at-rule-no-unknown` to ignore
two names that never appear, and the `@extend` they presumably wanted to allow
still errors.

The example is doubly misleading for the SCSS entry point, where
`scss/index.cjs` already sets `'at-rule-no-unknown': null` and delegates to
`scss/at-rule-no-unknown`.

## Impact

The one example in the README showing consumers how to extend the config
teaches a configuration that does not work. Someone debugging why `@extend`
still fails after following the docs loses time to a typo in the docs.

## Fix

Use an at-rule a reader plausibly needs to allow, and one that actually exists:

```diff
     "at-rule-no-unknown": [
       true,
       {
-        "ignoreAtRules": ["extends", "ignores"]
+        "ignoreAtRules": ["tailwind", "apply", "screen"]
       }
     ]
```

Add a sentence noting that SCSS consumers should configure
`scss/at-rule-no-unknown` instead, because `scss/index.cjs` disables the core
rule.

## Resolution
Replaced the nonexistent @extends/@ignores with tailwind/apply/screen and added a note directing SCSS consumers to scss/at-rule-no-unknown.
title: README 'Extending the config' example ignores at-rules that do not exist

body:
## Problem

The repository's own `.stylelintrc.json` extends the package it lives in:

```json
{
  "extends": [
    "@ivuorinen/stylelint-config/css"
  ]
}
```

That specifier does not resolve inside this repository, and no pipeline ever
tries.

## Evidence

No self-link exists under the `node-modules` linker this repo uses
(`.yarnrc.yml`: `nodeLinker: node-modules`):

```sh
$ ls -d node_modules/@ivuorinen/stylelint-config
ls: cannot access 'node_modules/@ivuorinen/stylelint-config': No such file or directory
$ ls -d node_modules/@ivuorinen/*
node_modules/@ivuorinen/config-checker
node_modules/@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config
```

Nothing invokes stylelint here either — `.mega-linter.yml` uses an allowlist and
`CSS_STYLELINT` is not on it:

```yaml
ENABLE_LINTERS:
  - YAML_YAMLLINT
  - MARKDOWN_MARKDOWNLINT
  - YAML_PRETTIER
  - JSON_PRETTIER
  - JAVASCRIPT_ES
  - TYPESCRIPT_ES
```

And there are no `.css` or `.scss` files in the repository to lint:
`find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type f -print` returns only `.cjs`,
`.mjs`, `.json`, `.yml`, `.md` and dotfiles.

## Impact

The file reads as dogfooding — the package linting itself with its own config —
but it is inert. Anyone who runs `npx stylelint` here to sanity-check a change
gets `Could not find "@ivuorinen/stylelint-config/css"` and may mistake it for a
regression in the package rather than a missing self-link. It is a decoy.

## Fix

Either make it real or delete it. Real version — self-reference by relative
path plus a fixture to lint, so the repo genuinely dogfoods:

```json
{
  "extends": ["./css/index.cjs"]
}
```

and add `CSS_STYLELINT` to `ENABLE_LINTERS` with a checked-in fixture. Cheaper
version, given `test/smoke.mjs` already lints real fixtures through all three
specifiers against a real install: delete `.stylelintrc.json` — the smoke test
covers strictly more.

## Resolution
Deleted the repo-root .stylelintrc.json. test/smoke.mjs already lints real fixtures through all three specifiers against a real install, which is strictly more coverage than the inert self-reference provided.
title: Repo-root .stylelintrc.json cannot resolve and is never executed

body:
## Problem

Two files in the repository configure behaviour against absent targets.

1. `.yamlignore` is empty.
2. `sync-labels.yml` filters on a label definition file that is not in the repo.

## Evidence

```sh
$ wc -c .yamlignore
0 .yamlignore

$ ls .github/labels.yml
ls: cannot access '.github/labels.yml': No such file or directory
```

`.github/workflows/sync-labels.yml`:
```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - master
    paths:
      - '.github/labels.yml'
      - '.github/workflows/sync-labels.yml'
```

The first `paths` entry can never match. The workflow still fires on its cron,
`workflow_dispatch`, and edits to itself, so label syncing works — the action
`ivuorinen/actions/sync-labels` evidently sources definitions elsewhere — but
the filter advertises a local file that is not there.

## Impact

Both are small false signals in the config surface. A zero-byte `.yamlignore`
suggests yamllint exclusions are configured when none are; the `paths` entry
suggests editing `.github/labels.yml` triggers a sync, so a contributor may
create that file expecting it to be honoured.

## Fix

```sh
git rm .yamlignore
```

and drop the dead path filter:

```diff
     paths:
-      - '.github/labels.yml'
       - '.github/workflows/sync-labels.yml'
```

If local label definitions *are* intended, add `.github/labels.yml` instead and
leave the filter.

## Resolution
Deleted the zero-byte .yamlignore and dropped the dead .github/labels.yml path filter from sync-labels.yml. The workflow still fires on cron, workflow_dispatch, workflow_call and edits to itself.
title: Two configuration surfaces reference targets that do not exist

body:
## Problem

`.gitignore` is an unedited concatenation of framework templates for stacks this
repository does not use, and one of its lines is not a valid pattern.

## Evidence

The repository contains four JavaScript files, a test, and config. `.gitignore`
carries entries for:

| stack | sample entries |
| --- | --- |
| PHP / Composer | `composer.phar`, `/vendor/`, `.php-cs-fixer.cache`, `.phpunit.result.cache` |
| Laravel | `bootstrap/compiled.php`, `app/storage/`, `public/hot`, `storage/*.key`, `Homestead.yaml`, `/.vagrant` |
| Next.js | `.next`, `next-env.d.ts`, `.vercel` |
| Nuxt / VuePress / Docusaurus | `.nuxt`, `.vuepress/dist`, `.docusaurus` |
| Serverless / DynamoDB | `.serverless/`, `.dynamodb/`, `.fusebox/` |
| JetBrains | ~30 `.idea/**` entries, `*.iws`, `atlassian-ide-plugin.xml` |
| Vim | `Session.vim`, `.netrwhist`, `[._]*.sw[a-p]` and four more glob classes |
| CMake | `cmake-build-*/` |
| Crashlytics | `com_crashlytics_export_strings.xml`, `fabric.properties` |

Line 70 is malformed:
```
!*.svg  # comment out if you don't need vector files
```

git has no trailing-comment syntax — a `#` is only a comment at the start of a
line. The whole string is therefore taken as one literal pattern, so the
intended `!*.svg` negation does not exist:

```sh
$ git check-ignore -v foo.svg
foo.svg NOT ignored          # no pattern matched at all, negation included
```

Harmless today because nothing ignores `*.svg`; it becomes a live bug the
moment a pattern does.

## Impact

Maintenance noise on a file people edit under time pressure: the two lines that
matter for this repo (`node_modules/`, `*.tgz` — the latter genuinely needed now
that `test/smoke.mjs` runs `npm pack`) are buried in ~200 irrelevant ones. The
malformed line is a latent trap, and duplicate entries (`/node_modules` and
`node_modules/`, `/coverage` and `coverage`, `out` and `out/`) show the file is
not being read when edited.

## Fix

Replace with what this repository actually produces:

```gitignore
node_modules/
.yarn/cache
.yarn/unplugged
.yarn/build-state.yml
.yarn/install-state.gz
.pnp.*

# npm pack artifacts from test/smoke.mjs
*.tgz

.stylelintcache
.eslintcache
*.log
.DS_Store
.env
.env*.local
```

If the JetBrains and Vim blocks are wanted, those belong in a global
`~/.config/git/ignore`, not in a shared repository.

## Resolution
Replaced the ~200-line multi-stack template with 20 lines covering what this repo produces. Verified node_modules/, *.tgz and .env are still ignored via git check-ignore. The malformed '!*.svg  # comment' pattern is gone.
title: .gitignore is a 200-line multi-stack template with one malformed pattern

body:
## Problem

The `Test` job body is identical in `.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml` and
`.github/workflows/publish.yml` — 22 lines of checkout, setup-node, and run
step, including the two pinned action SHAs.

## Evidence

Both files contain:

```yaml
  Test:
    name: Smoke Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read # to check out the repository

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js Environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"

      - name: Run smoke test
        shell: bash
        run: node test/smoke.mjs
```

The duplication is deliberate — `publish.yml` needs the job as a `needs:` gate
and cannot depend on a job in another workflow file — but it means two pinned
SHAs per action to keep in step.

## Impact

Renovate updates each occurrence independently. A partial update leaves PR
validation and release validation running different action versions, so a
change can pass on a PR and behave differently at release. Low probability,
annoying to diagnose.

## Fix

Extract a reusable workflow and call it from both. New
`.github/workflows/test.yml`:

```yaml
---
name: Smoke Test

on:
  workflow_call:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  Test:
    name: Smoke Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read # to check out the repository

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js Environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"

      - name: Run smoke test
        shell: bash
        run: node test/smoke.mjs
```

Then in both callers:

```yaml
  Test:
    name: Smoke Test
    uses: ./.github/workflows/test.yml
```

`publish.yml` keeps `needs: [Linter, Test]` unchanged. This matches the pattern
`stale.yml` and `sync-labels.yml` already anticipate with their `workflow_call`
triggers.

## Resolution
Extracted .github/workflows/test.yml as a workflow_call reusable; pr-lint.yml and publish.yml both now call it, so the pinned action SHAs exist once. publish.yml keeps needs: [Linter, Test]. actionlint exit 0, zizmor clean.
title: Smoke Test job is duplicated verbatim across two workflows

body:
## Problem

`package.json` carries a `gitHead` field:

```json
"gitHead": "23d15f15743fb59c1dbe658615ef2ed51c54d230",
```

`gitHead` is metadata npm injects into the *published* manifest at pack time.
It is not an input field, and a committed value is a leftover from a manual
`npm publish` run.

## Evidence

The recorded SHA is not reachable in this repository:

```sh
$ git cat-file -t 23d15f15743fb59c1dbe658615ef2ed51c54d230
fatal: Not a valid object name
```

It also sits between `repository` and `packageManager`, breaking the otherwise
alphabetical ordering of top-level keys that the rest of the manifest follows.

## Impact

Cosmetic but actively misleading: a reader may take it as the commit the
current version was built from. It is stale, unreachable, and npm overwrites it
on publish regardless.

## Fix

```diff
-  "gitHead": "23d15f15743fb59c1dbe658615ef2ed51c54d230",
```

Nothing reads it; removal is safe.

## Resolution
Removed the stale gitHead field from package.json.
title: Stale gitHead field committed in package.json

body:
## Problem

`scss/index.cjs` configures a rule with `null` as the primary option and a
populated secondary options object:

```js
'scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables': [null, { ignoreInsideAtRules: ['if', 'mixin'] }],
```

stylelint normalises any settings array whose primary option is `null` to
`null` — the rule is **off**, and `ignoreInsideAtRules` is dead configuration.
The shape reads as "enabled, with these exceptions".

## Evidence

Asked stylelint what it resolved the config to:

```js
const r = await stylelint.resolveConfig('x.scss', { config: scssConfig })
console.log(r.rules['scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables'])
```
```
scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables -> null
scss/at-mixin-named-arguments      -> null
scss/operator-no-unspaced          -> [true]
```

It resolves identically to the plain `null` on the line above it. The mechanism
is in `stylelint/lib/normalizeRuleSettings.mjs`:

```js
	const [primary, secondary] = rawSettings;

	if (rawSettings.length > 0 && (primary === null || primary === undefined)) {
		return null;
	}
```

The secondary element is discarded before it is ever read.

## Impact

The line misrepresents the config's intent. A maintainer reading it believes
duplicate `$variables` are rejected outside `@if`/`@mixin` blocks; nothing is
rejected. If the intent was to enable the rule with those exceptions, the
package has been shipping the opposite behaviour and nobody could tell from the
source.

## Fix

Decide which was meant and write it unambiguously.

If the rule should be **off** — matching current behaviour — drop the dead
options so the line says so:

```diff
-    'scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables': [null, { ignoreInsideAtRules: ['if', 'mixin'] }],
+    'scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables': null,
```

If it should be **on with those exceptions** — which the options suggest — the
primary option belongs in place of the `null`:

```diff
-    'scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables': [null, { ignoreInsideAtRules: ['if', 'mixin'] }],
+    'scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables': [true, { ignoreInsideAtRules: ['if', 'mixin'] }],
```

That second form is a behaviour change for SCSS consumers, so pair it with the
release note in `contract-a269f60f`. Either way, add a check to
`test/smoke.mjs` (see `tests-f84bc1e1`) so the enabled/disabled state of the
rule is asserted rather than assumed.

## Resolution
Collapsed to plain null with a comment recording that the secondary options never applied. Behaviour is unchanged deliberately; enabling the rule is a separate decision that would newly fail consumers' SCSS.
title: scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables is disabled while carrying live-looking options

body:
## Problem

`scripts/postinstall.cjs` logs three lines when it skips because
`@ivuorinen/config-checker` found a config, but says nothing at all when it
skips because the target file already exists — the path taken on every
reinstall.

```js
if (foundConfig.length > 0) {
  console.log('stylelint-config: Found existing stylelint config file, skipping creation.')
  console.log('stylelint-config: If you want to create a new config file, please remove the existing one.')
  console.log(`stylelint-config: Found config files at: ${foundConfig.join(', ')}`)
  process.exit(0)
}

const filePath = path.join(process.env.INIT_CWD, '.stylelintrc.json')
const fileConfigObject = {
  extends: ['@ivuorinen/stylelint-config/css']
}

if (!fs.existsSync(filePath)) {
  fs.writeFileSync(filePath, JSON.stringify(fileConfigObject, undefined, 2))
}
```

The `if (!fs.existsSync(filePath))` branch has no `else`, and the success case
has no log either.

## Evidence

Four distinct outcomes, two of them indistinguishable from the outside:

| outcome | signal |
| --- | --- |
| config-checker found a config | 3 log lines naming the files |
| `.stylelintrc.json` already exists | **nothing** |
| file written | **nothing** |
| `INIT_CWD` unset | uncaught `TypeError`, install aborts (`errors-767bc7a4`) |

Note the second row is unreachable-by-design overlap with the first —
`config-checker` detects `.stylelintrc.json` — but the branch exists and is the
documented behaviour in the README ("a `.stylelintrc.json` file will be created
automatically"), so a user who does not get one has no way to learn why.

## Impact

The README promises a file appears on install. When it does not, the install
output is silent about it, so the user cannot tell whether the script ran, was
skipped by `--ignore-scripts`, was blocked by npm's `allow-scripts` policy, or
decided not to write. Every other branch in the script logs; this one does not.

Relevant in practice: npm 11 now gates install scripts by default and prints
`npm warn allow-scripts @ivuorinen/stylelint-config@1.0.21 (postinstall: …)`,
so the "no file and no explanation" state is now the *default* first-install
experience.

## Fix

Log the write and the skip, so all outcomes are observable:

```js
if (fs.existsSync(filePath)) {
  console.log(`stylelint-config: ${filePath} already exists, leaving it alone.`)
  process.exit(0)
}

fs.writeFileSync(filePath, JSON.stringify(fileConfigObject, undefined, 2))
console.log(`stylelint-config: wrote ${filePath}`)
```

Also add a README note that npm 11 may block the postinstall and that the file
can be created by hand — see the `docs` lens.

## Resolution
postinstall now logs every outcome through a single log() helper: INIT_CWD missing, opt-out set, unreadable manifest, transitive install, existing config found, file already present, and the successful write. Documented in the README, including the npm 11 allow-scripts gate.
title: postinstall's most common outcome is silent

body:
## Problem

`svg-tags@1.0.0` reaches the published dependency closure and carries no
`license` field in its `package.json`. The project itself is correctly licensed
(MIT in both `package.json` and `LICENSE.md`), and every other package in the
tree is permissive, so this is the only gap.

## Evidence

Scanned every installed manifest for a missing or non-string `license`:

```
NO LICENSE FIELD: qrcode-terminal@0.12.0
NO LICENSE FIELD: svg-tags@1.0.0
```

Reachability separates them — only one is in the runtime path:

```sh
$ yarn why svg-tags
└─ stylelint@npm:17.6.0
   └─ svg-tags@npm:1.0.0 (via npm:^1.0.0)

$ yarn why qrcode-terminal
└─ npm@npm:11.11.0
   └─ qrcode-terminal@npm:0.12.0 (via npm:^0.12.0)
```

`qrcode-terminal` arrives via `npm`, pulled in by
`@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` — a `devDependency`, so it never ships.
`svg-tags` arrives via `stylelint`, which is currently a hard `dependency`
(`deps-d7bddd01`), so it is in every consumer's tree.

Everything else is permissive. The only non-MIT license in the whole tree is
`Python-2.0` (`argparse`), which is MIT-compatible, and a copyleft scan for
`GPL|AGPL|LGPL|SSPL|BUSL|CDDL|EPL|MPL|CC-BY-SA|Commons-Clause` returned nothing.

## Impact

Low but real for anyone running license compliance over their dependency tree:
`svg-tags` will surface as `UNKNOWN`, and an unknown license is conventionally
treated as "all rights reserved" by automated gates. Consumers with a
license-allowlist CI step will see this package as the path that introduced it.

## Fix

This is not fixable in this repository's own manifests — it is upstream in
`svg-tags`, reached through `stylelint`. Two concrete actions:

1. Record the accepted exception so the next audit and any consumer gate can
   see it was reviewed rather than missed. Add to `README.md` or a new
   `NOTICE.md`:
   ```markdown
   ## License notes

   `svg-tags@1.0.0`, reached transitively via `stylelint`, ships no `license`
   field in its `package.json`. Its repository states MIT
   (https://github.com/element-io/svg-tags). Recorded here so license-scanning
   consumers can allowlist it deliberately.
   ```
2. Reduce the blast radius by moving stylelint to `peerDependencies`
   (`deps-d7bddd01`) — `svg-tags` then arrives through the consumer's own
   stylelint, which they already own, instead of through this package.

## Resolution
Added a 'Dependency license note' section to the README recording svg-tags@1.0.0's missing license field, its stated MIT license, and that it is reached via stylelint. Blast radius also reduced by deps-d7bddd01: with stylelint now a peer, svg-tags arrives through the consumer's own stylelint install.
title: One runtime-closure dependency declares no license

body:
## Problem

`package.json` lists `"postcss": "^8.5.8"` under `dependencies`. Nothing in the
published package imports it.

## Evidence

```sh
scripts/postinstall.cjs:9:const checkConfig = require('@ivuorinen/config-checker')
test/smoke.mjs:10-16: node:assert/strict, node:child_process, node:fs, node:os,
                      node:path, node:process, node:url
```

The only `postcss` hit in the whole shipped surface is the word "postcss"
inside a comment. `files` in `package.json` is `["css/*","scss/*","scripts/*"]`,
so that grep covers everything that ships.

postcss is already in the tree without this declaration — it arrives as a real
dependency of `stylelint-order@8.1.1` (`dependencies: {"postcss": "^8.5.8"}`)
and as a peer of `stylelint-config-recommended-scss@17`
(`peerDependencies: {"postcss": "^8.3.3"}`).

## Impact

The declaration makes `@ivuorinen/stylelint-config` the attributed dependent
for postcss advisories — see `security-9f718b34`, where
`yarn npm audit` reports `Dependents: @ivuorinen/stylelint-config@workspace:.`
for GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849. It creates an obligation to track postcss releases for
a package that never calls postcss, and it pins a floor (`^8.5.8`) that can
conflict with a consumer's own resolution for no reason.

## Fix

Remove the line:

```diff
   "dependencies": {
     "@ivuorinen/config-checker": "^2.2.1",
-    "postcss": "^8.5.8",
     "stylelint-config-recommended-scss": "^17.0.0",
```

Then `yarn install` to refresh the lockfile and re-run `test/smoke.mjs` to
confirm both specifiers still lint (postcss remains present transitively, so
nothing should change).

## Resolution
WRONG FINDING. postcss is not an unused dependency. It is declared to satisfy stylelint-config-recommended-scss's peerDependencies {postcss: ^8.3.3} — a config package must provide its own dependencies' peers. Removing it was attempted and yarn rejected it: 'YN0002: @ivuorinen/stylelint-config@workspace:. doesn't provide postcss (p6a9fdb), requested by stylelint-config-recommended-scss.' The grep-for-imports test was the wrong instrument for a peer-forwarding dependency. postcss is retained; only its floor was raised to ^8.5.18 under security-9f718b34.
title: postcss is declared as a direct dependency but never imported

body:
## Problem

The fix for `complexity-512b6f2d` extracted the smoke test into a
`workflow_call` reusable and had both workflows call it. The calling job was
written as:

```yaml
  Test:
    name: Smoke Test
    uses: ./.github/workflows/test.yml
```

Both callers declare `permissions: {}` at file scope. A called workflow cannot
be granted more than its caller holds, and `test.yml`'s job requests
`contents: read`. That exceeds an empty grant, so GitHub rejected the workflow
before creating any job.

## Evidence

`Lint Code Base` was `startup_failure` on every commit of the branch, while the
same workflow succeeded on `main` and on an unrelated Renovate PR:

```text
startup_failure  pull_request  fix/clean-install-and-audit-remediation
startup_failure  pull_request  fix/clean-install-and-audit-remediation
success          push          main
success          pull_request  renovate/npm-brace-expansion-vulnerability
startup_failure  pull_request  fix/clean-install-and-audit-remediation
```

The failure produced nothing to read — no logs (`failed to get run log: log not
found`), no annotations (HTTP 404), and zero jobs:

```text
gh api .../actions/runs/<id>/jobs --jq '.total_count'
0
```

Consequence: `PR Lint` and `Smoke Test` never appeared in `gh pr checks`, so the
release gate added by this branch had never executed once. Only CodeQL,
SonarCloud, Snyk and CodeRabbit were reporting, and all of them were green —
the branch looked fully validated while its own test gate had never run.

## Impact

Worse than the duplication it replaced. A `needs:` gate that fails at startup
does not block anything: `publish.yml` lists `Test` in `needs`, but a workflow
that never starts produces no failing status for a branch protection rule to
catch. The fix for a maintainability finding silently disabled a correctness
gate.

The reason it went unnoticed is the real lesson. `complexity-512b6f2d` was
resolved on the evidence "actionlint exit 0, zizmor clean". Both tools parse
workflow syntax; neither evaluates the permissions relationship between a caller
and a called workflow, so neither could ever have caught this. Local linters
were treated as sufficient evidence for a change whose failure mode is only
observable server-side.

## Fix

Widen the grant at the call site in both `pr-lint.yml` and `publish.yml`:

```yaml
  Test:
    name: Smoke Test
    permissions:
      contents: read # to check out the repository
    uses: ./.github/workflows/test.yml
```

Verified server-side rather than locally — the run for the fixing commit created
jobs where every previous run created none:

```text
job count: 2
  PR Lint: in_progress
  Smoke Test / Smoke Test: success
```

For any future change to workflow wiring, confirm against an actual run: a
green local `actionlint` says the YAML parses, not that the workflow starts.

## Resolution
Granted contents: read on the calling Test job in both pr-lint.yml and publish.yml. Confirmed server-side rather than locally: the pr-lint run for 736fb26 created 2 jobs (PR Lint, Smoke Test) where every earlier run on this branch created 0, and Smoke Test passed — its first successful execution on this branch.
title: Reusable-workflow extraction failed at startup on every commit, unnoticed

body:
## Problem

`releaseRules` in `@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` keys release decisions on
the commit **scope**, but Renovate emits two different scopes for the same class
of change. The same file, changed the same way, produces no release, a patch, or
a minor depending on which scope the bot happened to use.

```json
"releaseRules": [
  { "breaking": true, "type": "chore", "scope": "deps",    "release": "minor" },
  {                   "type": "chore", "scope": "deps",    "release": "patch" },
  {                   "type": "chore", "scope": "actions", "release": false   }
]
```

## Evidence

`actions/cache` bumps in this repository's own history, all three scopes in use:

```text
chore(actions): update actions/cache action (v6.0.0 → v6.1.0) (#163)   -> release: false  -> no release
chore(deps):    update actions/cache action (v5.0.2 → v5.0.3) (#97)    -> release: patch  -> patch
chore(deps)!:   update actions/cache action (v5.0.5 → v6.0.0) (#162)   -> release: minor  -> v1.2.0
```

`actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-node` show the same split:

```text
chore(actions): update actions/checkout action (v7.0.0 → v7.0.1) (#175)
chore(deps)!:   update actions/checkout action (v6.0.3 → v7.0.0) (#159)
chore(actions): update actions/setup-node action (v6.3.0 → v6.4.0) (#147)
chore(deps)!:   update actions/setup-node action (v6.4.0 → v7.0.0) (#168)
```

Three of the last four minor releases were caused **entirely** by GitHub Action
version bumps:

```text
v1.1.0  d60ed3b  chore(deps)!: update actions/checkout action (v6.0.3 → v7.0.0)
v1.2.0  44f9b08  chore(deps)!: update actions/cache action (v5.0.5 → v6.0.0)
v1.3.0  2a7ab7d  chore(deps)!: update actions/setup-node action (v6.4.0 → v7.0.0)
```

None of those can affect a consumer. `files` is
`["css/*", "scss/*", "scripts/*"]`, so `.github/workflows/**` is not in the
published tarball — the artifact at v1.2.0 is byte-identical to v1.1.2 apart
from the version field.

The rule also runs the other way. Renovate labels a change to this package's
**own declared support range** with the same `chore(deps)!` prefix:

```text
$ git show 986a6a9 -- package.json
-    "stylelint": "^16.26.1",
+    "stylelint": "^17.0.0",
```

`986a6a9 chore(deps)!: update stylelint (16.26.1 → 17.0.0) (#87)`

Under `{breaking: true, type: chore, scope: deps, release: "minor"}` that
consumer-facing support change also releases as a minor. The rule cannot
distinguish "bumped a CI action" from "dropped support for a stylelint major",
because the distinction is in *which files changed*, not in the message.

## Impact

1. **Version inflation.** Consumers see minor releases with identical
   payloads and changelogs full of CI noise, so the version number stops
   signalling anything about the package.
2. **Under-versioning of real breaks.** A genuine support-range change ships as
   a minor. A consumer on `^1.x` pinned to stylelint 16 can receive a config
   that requires stylelint 17 without a major bump — and, because stylelint is
   a hard dependency rather than a peer (`deps-d7bddd01`), without an install
   warning either.
3. **Non-determinism.** Whether a release happens at all depends on Renovate's
   scope choice, which is not under this repo's control.

## Fix

Stop keying releases on scope, and restrict release-triggering paths instead.
Renovate's config is the right place, because it knows which manager produced
the change. In `.github/renovate.json`, force the scope per manager:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": ["github>ivuorinen/renovate-config"],
  "packageRules": [
    {
      "matchManagers": ["github-actions", "pre-commit"],
      "semanticCommitType": "chore",
      "semanticCommitScope": "actions"
    },
    {
      "matchManagers": ["npm"],
      "semanticCommitType": "chore",
      "semanticCommitScope": "deps"
    }
  ]
}
```

With scopes made deterministic, the existing `releaseRules` become correct:
`chore(actions)` never releases, `chore(deps)` releases patch, and a genuinely
breaking npm change is written by hand as `fix!:`/`feat!:` so it takes the
preset's default major.

Then drop the `{breaking: true, type: chore, scope: deps, release: "minor"}`
rule — with actions excluded, a breaking npm dependency change should not be
downgraded from major.

Verify with a dry run before trusting it:

```sh
npx semantic-release --dry-run --no-ci
```

## Correction to the Fix above (2026-07-27)

The `## Fix` section stands, but the earlier "not applied" note that followed it
was wrong twice over and is replaced by this.

**It claimed `semanticCommitType`/`semanticCommitScope` are invalid inside
`packageRules`.** They are not. That was inferred from the JSON schema listing
only `match*`-style keys under `packageRules.items.allOf[0].properties`, but
`additionalProperties` is undefined at both levels — absence of a key is not
prohibition. Renovate's own default presets use `semanticCommitType` inside
`packageRules`:

```json
{
  "packageRules": [
    { "matchPackageNames": ["*"], "semanticCommitType": "chore" },
    { "matchDepTypes": ["dependencies", "require"], "semanticCommitType": "fix" }
  ]
}
```

**It also dismissed the validator's pass.** `renovate-config-validator` reported
"validated successfully", and that was waved away because the run said
"Validating .github/renovate.json as global config" — the looser mode. Validating
a file named `renovate.json` in the working directory exercises repo-config
rules instead, and it still passes, while a deliberately bogus key is rejected:

```text
$ npx renovate-config-validator     # with semanticCommitType + semanticCommitScope
 INFO: Config validated successfully against 1 file(s)

$ npx renovate-config-validator     # with "totallyNotARealOption": "x"
ERROR: Found errors in configuration
       "message": "Invalid configuration option: packageRules[0].totallyNotARealOption"
```

The validator does check `packageRules` keys. The config is valid.

## Scope narrowed by the maintainer

The original Fix proposed making scopes deterministic for both managers and
dropping the `{breaking: true, type: chore, scope: deps, release: "minor"}`
rule. The maintainer's instruction is narrower and does not require the second
half: GitHub Actions updates must always be `chore(actions):` and must never
bump the version whatever their size, unless the PR title is changed by hand.

That is satisfied without touching `.releaserc.json` at all, because the shared
`{type: chore, scope: actions, release: false}` rule already absorbs the
breaking marker. Verified by running `@semantic-release/commit-analyzer` with
this repository's real `releaseRules`:

```text
  NO RELEASE  <- chore(actions): update actions/checkout action (v7.0.0 → v7.0.1)
  NO RELEASE  <- chore(actions)!: update actions/checkout action (v6.0.3 → v7.0.0)
  NO RELEASE  <- chore(actions): update actions/checkout action (v6 → v7) + BREAKING CHANGE footer
  patch       <- chore(deps): update actions/cache action (v5.0.2 → v5.0.3)
  minor       <- chore(deps)!: update actions/cache action (v5.0.5 → v6.0.0)
```

So the whole defect reduces to Renovate sometimes labelling an action update
`chore(deps)`. Pinning the scope closes it, and no suppression of the `!` is
needed.

## Applied fix

`.github/renovate.json`:

```json
"packageRules": [
  {
    "matchManagers": ["github-actions"],
    "semanticCommitType": "chore",
    "semanticCommitScope": "actions"
  }
]
```

The manual override works natively: `allow_merge_commit=false` and
`allow_rebase_merge=false`, so squash is this repository's only merge method,
and `squash_merge_commit_title=COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE`. A multi-commit PR takes the
PR title as its commit subject, so retitling a Renovate PR
`feat: …` or `fix: …` releases deliberately.

## Not covered

`pre-commit` hook updates have the same property — they never reach the
published tarball, and `chore(deps): update pre-commit hook
igorshubovych/markdownlint-cli` has released patches (v1.0.33, v1.3.1). They are
left alone because the instruction named GitHub Actions specifically. Adding
`"pre-commit"` to `matchManagers` would extend the same treatment.

Also still true, and not addressed here: the
`{breaking: true, type: chore, scope: deps, release: "minor"}` rule downgrades a
genuinely breaking npm dependency change to a minor. That rule lives in
`@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` and has to change there.

## Resolution
Pinned github-actions and pre-commit updates to chore(actions) in .github/renovate.json, so the shared releaseRule {type: chore, scope: actions, release: false} matches every time. Verified with the real commit-analyzer that the rule also suppresses chore(actions)! and a BREAKING CHANGE footer, so no handling of the breaking marker is needed and .releaserc.json is untouched. Manual override works natively: squash is the only merge method and squash_merge_commit_title is COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE. Two corrections recorded in the finding: semanticCommitType/Scope ARE valid in packageRules (Renovate's own default presets use them; absence from the JSON schema's properties is not prohibition when additionalProperties is unset), and the earlier validator pass was wrongly dismissed because it had run in global-config mode. The remaining half — breaking chore(deps) downgraded to minor — is upstream in @ivuorinen/semantic-release-config and is filed separately.
title: Identical changes release under three different rules depending on an arbitrary scope
